A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HardcoreLogic benchmark. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices are sufficiently complete and readable for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, solver-complexity measurements, error analyses, and Hitori and Skyscraper experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and reports additional complexity-performance, annotation-agreement, and regression-sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction framework, transformation operations, and puzzle-solving interface are retained. Expanded unsolvable-puzzle recipes document variants already present in v1; auxiliary-model configurations and annotation changes concern experimental implementation and evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same ten games, six puzzle categories, and solvable and unsolvable transformations. Table 1 retains 1,389 Original and 5,250 HardcoreLogic puzzles. The added analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 7 and the main comparisons retain the same 21 evaluated models. The additional annotators, including Claude Sonnet 4.5, serve the labeling procedure rather than becoming benchmark comparators.

E3.justification: Error annotation changes from GPT-5 to three-model majority voting with manual adjudication, and Table 8 revises Faithfulness into Over Verification. New evaluation controls include Original-error sampling and single-factor regression refitting. Appendix A also changes the reported clue-translation and verification models, without establishing dataset regeneration.

E4.justification: v3 adds Original-versus-HardcoreLogic error comparisons, complexity-performance correlations, annotation-consistency checks, and single-factor regression sensitivity analysis in Section 4.2 and Appendices D.1, D.3, and D.5. The earlier Hitori and Skyscraper analyses remain as D.2 and D.4.

E5.justification: v3 introduces correlation significance tests, regression coefficient confidence intervals and p-values, and Fleiss' and Cohen's Kappa agreement reporting. These substantially expand statistical validation beyond v1. The existing four-runs-per-instance protocol remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Substantial new correlation, agreement, and regression-sensitivity results accompany revised error distributions. For example, Kimi's factual-error share in Figure 7 changes from 40% to 58% under revised annotation; unsolvability distributions also change. Main accuracy results and the existing Hitori and Skyscraper scores are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the regression intercept from the average Original accuracy to the fitted prediction with no transformations, elaborated in Appendix D.5. This is a limited mathematical correction; the displayed regression equation otherwise restates the existing additive model, and Table 5's formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the benchmark's scope, claims about failures on unfamiliar puzzles, and contributions from error analysis and scalable construction. Additional analyses support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect rule perturbations to understanding failures, Kimi's skipped reasoning steps to factual errors, and Sudoku regression sensitivity to heterogeneous UE1 subtypes. The unsolvability discussion removes Kimi from examples of models prone to unjustified judgments. The broader interpretation of limited reasoning robustness remains.

D1.justification: Table 3 expands construction and verification details for existing unsolvable variants. v3 newly specifies 600 sampled closed-source cases and 50 responses for unsolvability sufficiency analysis, and updates auxiliary-model identities. These improve documentation without establishing larger samples or regenerated data; prompt templates and benchmark/code access links remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the de Moura and Bjørner Z3 reference. Research positioning remains substantially unchanged; publication updates for Enigmata, ZebraLogic, SATBench, and the chameleon evaluation paper refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Editing is localized: terminology changes from mutation to variation, explanations are expanded, and author, acknowledgment, and conference information are updated. New appendix subsections extend the document, while most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual presentation with the error comparison in Figure 8, puzzle illustrations in Figure 11, complexity curves in Figures 12–14, and sensitivity/confidence-interval displays in Figure 15. It also adds statistical and agreement tables, expands Table 3, revises legends, and adopts conference formatting.

improvement.justification: The added complexity-performance checks, regression sensitivity analysis, confidence intervals, and construction details address validation and documentation gaps in v1. However, interpretation remains imperfect: Section 4.2 retains a roughly 50% Kimi error-share claim although Figure 7 now gives 36%, and Appendix D.3 claims generally high agreement despite an overall UP-sufficiency Kappa of 0.27. The added scrutiny and transparency provide a limited net improvement.
